content: 1. Clarithromycin tablets (Biaxin Film-tab) and oral suspension (Biaxin Granules) can be administered with or without food. 2. Clarithromycin extended-release tablets (Biaxin XL Film-tab) must be taken with food. These tablets should be swallowed whole and must not be chewed, broken, or crushed. Adult Dosage Guidelines: For pharyngitis or tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes: Administer 250 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 10 days. For acute maxillary sinusitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and/or Streptococcus pneumoniae: Administer 500 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 14 days, or Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 14 days. For acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and/or Streptococcus pneumoniae: Administer 500 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7–14 days, or Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis caused by Haemophilus parainfluenzae: Administer 500 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days, or Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For community-acquired pneumonia caused by Haemophilus influenzae: Administer 250 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days, or Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For community-acquired pneumonia caused by Haemophilus parainfluenzae and/or Moraxella catarrhalis: Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, and/or Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Administer 250 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7–14 days, or Administer two 500 mg Biaxin XL tablets once daily (q24h) for 7 days. For uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes: Administer 250 mg of Biaxin tablets every 12 hours (q12h) for 7 days. Helicobacter pylori Eradication to Reduce the Risk of Duodenal Ulcer Recurrence: Clarithromycin/Lansoprazole/Amoxicillin: The recommended adult dose is 500 mg clarithromycin, 30 mg lansoprazole, and 1 gram amoxicillin, all administered twice daily (q12h) for 10 or 14 days. Clarithromycin/Omeprazole/Amoxicillin: The recommended adult dose is 500 mg clarithromycin, 20 mg omeprazole, and 1 gram amoxicillin, all administered twice daily (q12h) for 10 days. For patients with an ulcer present at the start of therapy, an additional 18 days of omeprazole 20 mg once daily is recommended for ulcer healing and symptom relief. Clarithromycin/Omeprazole: The recommended adult dose is 500 mg clarithromycin three times daily (q8h) and 40 mg omeprazole once daily (qAM) for 14 days. An additional 14 days of omeprazole 20 mg once daily is recommended for ulcer healing and symptom relief. Clarithromycin/Ranitidine Bismuth Citrate: The recommended adult dose is 500 mg clarithromycin given twice daily (q12h) or three times daily (q8h) and 400 mg ranitidine bismuth citrate given twice daily (q12h) for 14 days. An additional 14 days of 400 mg ranitidine bismuth citrate twice daily is recommended for ulcer healing and symptom relief. This combination therapy is not recommended for patients with creatinine clearance less than 25 mL/min. Pediatric Dosage: The usual recommended daily dosage is 15 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (q12h) for 10 days. Clarithromycin can be administered without dosage adjustment in the presence of hepatic impairment if renal function is normal. In cases of severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min), with or without coexisting hepatic impairment, the dose should be halved or the dosing interval doubled. Mycobacterial Infections: Prophylaxis: No studies have been conducted in pediatric populations for Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) prophylaxis. Doses recommended for prophylaxis are derived from MAC treatment studies in children. Treatment: Clarithromycin is the primary agent for treating disseminated infections due to MAC. It should be used in combination with other antimycobacterial drugs that demonstrate in vitro activity against MAC or clinical benefit in MAC treatment. Therapy should continue for life if clinical and microbiological improvements are observed. Constituting Instructions for Oral Suspension: 1. Add half the required volume of water to the bottle and shake vigorously. 2. Add the remaining water and shake again. 3. Shake well before each use. 4. The oversized bottle allows space for shaking. 5. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Do not refrigerate. 6. After mixing, store at 15°C to 30°C (59°F to 86°F) and use within 14 days.
